summary: Panama is visa-free for well over a hundred nationalities — including the whole EU, the UK, the US, Canada and most of Latin America — with tourist stays of up to 90 days. Everyone else needs either a stamped consular visa or, for a restricted list of nationalities, an authorized visa cleared in advance by the National Immigration Service; a valid visa or residence permit from Canada, the US, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the UK, Singapore or an EU country replaces the Panamanian visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Under Executive Decree 521 of 6 August 2018, anyone whose nationality needs a Panamanian visa may enter as a tourist without one if they hold a valid visa or residence permit issued by Canada, the United States, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom, Singapore or any European Union member state; the decree names the EU, not the Schengen area. The 2018 decree also required the visa to be multiple-entry, already used in the issuing country and valid for at least six more months; Executive Decree 196 of 28 October 2024 replaced that with one condition, that the visa be valid on arrival in Panama. The decrees exclude no nationality and do not state a length of stay; Panama's tourist limit is 90 days.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Panama?
faq.answer: For most travelers, no. Panama waives visas for well over a hundred nationalities, including all EU and Schengen states, the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel and most of South and Central America — tourists may stay up to 90 days. Everyone else needs a stamped visa from a consulate, or an authorized visa cleared in advance if their nationality is on Panama's restricted list.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Panama as a tourist?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt visitors may stay up to 90 days — the limit Panama's immigration law (Decreto Ley 3 of 2008, art. 16) sets for tourists, unless an international agreement provides otherwise. If you were granted fewer than 90 days, you can apply to the Servicio Nacional de Migración before they run out for an extension up to a maximum stay of 90 days.

faq.question: Can I enter Panama with a US or Schengen visa instead of a Panamanian one?
faq.answer: Yes, if it comes from the right country. Executive Decree 521 of 2018 lets anyone whose nationality needs a Panamanian visa enter as a tourist with a valid visa or residence permit from Canada, the United States, Australia, South Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom, Singapore or any EU member state. Since Executive Decree 196 of 2024 the visa only has to be valid on arrival; it no longer has to be multiple-entry or already used. The decrees exclude no nationality and do not say how long you may stay; Panama's tourist limit is 90 days.

faq.question: What is the difference between a stamped visa and an authorized visa?
faq.answer: A stamped visa (visa estampada) is issued by a Panamanian consulate. An authorized visa (visa autorizada) applies to a restricted list of nationalities and must first be approved by the National Immigration Service in Panama. Panama does not publish processing times for either.

faq.question: Do I need to show money to enter Panama?
faq.answer: Yes. Panama's migration service requires proof of economic solvency consistent with your declared stay and never less than B/.500 (USD 500), alongside a confirmed reservation to leave the country within the permitted period. Children under 18 do not need to show funds.

faq.question: What currency does Panama use?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency is the balboa (PAB), used interchangeably with the US dollar. Because of counterfeit US$50 and US$100 bills, it advises carrying only small US notes.
